title: Redmi Buds 6 Play: Cheap, Long-Lasting Earbuds for Everyday Listening
summary: The Redmi Buds 6 Play are Xiaomi's cheapest true wireless earbuds: 3.6 g per bud, up to 36 hours with the case, Bluetooth 5.4 and IPX4 — but no active noise cancellation. Here's who they suit and what's missing.
description:
## Who is it for?

- Students and first-time wireless earbud buyers.
- Anyone who wants a cheap backup pair.
- Everyday music, video, classes and calls.

## Why consider it?

- Up to 36 hours total battery (Xiaomi).
- Only 3.6 g per earbud.
- Bluetooth 5.4, Google Fast Pair, EQ presets in the app.

sections.title: What are the Redmi Buds 6 Play?
sections.content: The Redmi Buds 6 Play (model M2420E1) are the entry model in Xiaomi's Redmi Buds 6 line, sold in many markets including the UK, EU, Australia, the Middle East and Africa. They come in black, white, blue and pink, and compete with no-name earbuds on price while offering an app and a recognised brand.

sections.title: Design and comfort
sections.content: Xiaomi lists 3.6 g per earbud and 40 g for the whole set, so they are easy to carry and comfortable for long sessions. The bean shape sits in the ear without pressing on the outer ear. IPX4 means sweat and splashes are fine; swimming is not.

sections.title: Sound and app
sections.content: Each bud uses a 10 mm dynamic driver. Expect a punchy, consumer-friendly tuning suitable for pop, podcasts and video rather than critical listening. The Xiaomi Earbuds app offers five EQ presets (standard, bass boost, voice boost, treble boost, volume boost). Xiaomi doesn't list AAC or LDAC, so assume SBC.

sections.title: Battery, calls and connectivity
sections.content: Battery is the standout: Xiaomi rates up to 7.5 hours per charge and 36 hours with the case (measured at 50% volume), and a 10-minute charge gives about 3 hours. AI noise reduction cleans up your voice on calls but does not reduce what you hear — there is no ANC. Bluetooth 5.4 and Google Fast Pair make pairing easy on Android; Xiaomi lists a low-latency mode of about 180 ms, fine for video but noticeable in competitive games.

sections.title: Who should buy them — and who shouldn't
sections.content: Buy them if you want cheap, light earbuds with long battery life for daily listening and calls. Skip them if you need ANC, low latency for competitive games, multipoint or high-quality codecs — look at the SoundPEATS T3 Pro or a higher Redmi Buds model instead.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used these earbuds in person. This is a research roundup based on Xiaomi's global and regional product pages and specifications, plus retailer price listings, checked November 2026. Battery and latency figures are Xiaomi's, not our measurements. Images are official Xiaomi product photos.

sections.title: Should you buy the Redmi Buds 6 Play?
sections.content: For everyday use on a minimal budget, yes: long battery life, light buds, Bluetooth 5.4, an EQ app and IPX4 from a major brand. Just don't expect ANC, transparency or gaming-grade latency.

pros: Long battery life: up to 36 h with the case (Xiaomi).
Fast charging: 10 minutes for about 3 hours.
App with 5 EQ presets and touch customisation.
Very low price for a major brand.
cons: No active noise cancellation or transparency mode.
About 180 ms latency is noticeable in fast games.
Bean shape may not stay put during intense workouts.
Fast Pair only works on Android.

faq.question: Do the Redmi Buds 6 Play have ANC?
faq.answer: No. AI noise reduction only cleans up your voice on calls.

faq.question: How long does the battery last?
faq.answer: Xiaomi rates up to 7.5 hours per charge and 36 hours with the case at 50% volume.

faq.question: Do they work with iPhone?
faq.answer: Yes, over standard Bluetooth. Google Fast Pair is Android-only.

faq.question: Are they good for gaming?
faq.answer: Fine for casual games and video; the roughly 180 ms latency is noticeable in shooters and rhythm games.

faq.question: Can they connect to two devices at once?
faq.answer: Xiaomi doesn't list multipoint, so assume one device at a time.

faq.question: Redmi Buds 6 Play or SoundPEATS T3 Pro?
faq.answer: Choose the Redmi for battery life and low price; the SoundPEATS T3 Pro if you want ANC and transparency.
